reader.requirement: At --std 85 a format 1 REPLACE statement whose pseudo-text-1 holds no text word (empty, spaces only, or only comment lines) must be refused; a pseudo-text-1 holding one or more text words is accepted (the comma/semicolon-only case is the sibling SR7, refused by the same test).
reader.edition-search: Read ScreenOperandPair (the PseudoText1 test from.MatchWords.Count == 0 is unconditional), the REPLACE arm that builds OperandScreen(ReplaceOperandRules, ..., edition), and TextWord.IsSpaceForMatching (kind-only). The edition the screen carries is read only by the character, partial-word (ConstructRegistry ReplacingPartialWord2002), word-operand and length checks, none of which decides SR3; the ALSO/LAST and REPLACE-placement gates on the statement are other rules.

reader.notes: One edition-blind test implements the rule for both COPY and REPLACE. At --std 85 the message cites §2023:7.2.4.3 SR3 (whose wording folds 1985 SR3 and SR7 together) rather than §1985:XII.3.3 SR3; a message-text matter only.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the 1985 text-word definition (III, Text Word, item 3 excludes comment lines and the word COPY) and REPLACE GR8 (debugging lines in pseudo-text take part in matching as if the D were absent). rep_copy.cob REPLACE ==COPY== BY ==WS-A==: refused at 85 (COBOL2451/COBOL2449, exit 65), so the COPY-only pseudo-text-1 is not admitted, though the refusal comes through the COPY scanner, not COBOL2572. rep_debug.cob, whose pseudo-text-1 is only a D line holding WS-A, without WITH DEBUGGING MODE: accepted, matched, and printed BBBB, as GR8 requires. rep_paren.cob REPLACE ==(== BY ==(==: a parenthesis is always a text word, accepted, printed Q. cite.py: OK  §1985:XII.3.3 SR3  (║3.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR3; OK  §1985:XII.3.4 GR8  (║3.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR8.
